key_insight: Clinical Consensus Selection (CCS) improves radiology report generation by choosing the best report from multiple sampled candidates rather than relying on a model’s default single output.
clinical_relevance: This could make AI-generated radiology reports more clinically reliable at inference time, especially by better capturing findings that matter for downstream review.
method: Sample multiple candidate reports from a radiology multimodal LLM.
Score candidates using both text-based agreement and an image-report multimodal utility.
Select the report with the highest clinical consensus across the pool.
evidence_signal: Across three datasets and multiple radiology MLLMs, CCS outperformed single-path decoding and generic Best-of-N baselines, with especially strong gains on clinical metrics.
watch_item: Because CCS depends on extra sampling and selection at inference time, it may increase compute cost and its utility could vary with the quality of the multimodal embedder.
paper_title: CCS: Clinical Consensus Selection for Radiology Report Generation
